VirtualDairyHerdR: A Digital Dairy Herd Simulator for Education, Research and Precision Livestock Farming

Source: R/VirtualDairyHerdR-package.R
VirtualDairyHerdR-package.Rd

VirtualDairyHerdR generates biologically realistic synthetic dairy herd datasets for teaching statistics, data wrangling, visualisation, and machine learning in agricultural and precision livestock farming contexts.

It is part of the Farmaverse — an open ecosystem of R livestock simulation packages inspired by the pharmaverse.

Simulation pipeline

Functions are designed to chain together, each accepting the output of the previous step and adding columns:

simulate_farm()
    └── simulate_herd()
            ├── simulate_milk()
            │       ├── simulate_mastitis()
            │       └── simulate_fertility()
            └── simulate_activity()

Main functions

simulate_farm()

Create a farm-level configuration object.

simulate_herd()

Generate a synthetic dairy herd.

simulate_lactation()

Wood's lactation curve engine.

simulate_milk()

Daily milk yield, fat, protein, and SCC.

simulate_mastitis()

Mastitis disease effects and labels.

simulate_fertility()

Conception probability and days open.

simulate_activity()

Activity score, steps, lying/standing time.

education_summary()

Flexible grouped summary table.

Bundled datasets

demo_herd

200-cow synthetic herd with milk production data.

demo_mastitis

Same herd with mastitis labels at 15% prevalence.

Design principles

  1. Biologically grounded — parameters drawn from published dairy science literature and real sensor platform experience.

  2. Pipeline-first — every function accepts the output of the previous step and adds columns.

  3. Education-ready — datasets designed to support teaching statistics, data wrangling, visualisation, and machine learning.

  4. Transparent — all simulation logic is open, documented, and auditable.

  5. Interoperable — standard tibbles; works with tidyverse, ggplot2, caret, tidymodels, and mlr3.

Reproducibility

Every simulation function accepts a seed argument. Pass the same seed to reproduce identical datasets across sessions. All outputs carry synthetic_data = TRUE so they can never be mistaken for real farm records.

References

Wood, P.D.P. (1967). Algebraic model of the lactation curve in cattle. Nature, 216, 164–165.
